bibl.title: A Wax Effigy Pierced by Three Bones: The Pharaonic Origins of a Late-Antique Cursing Ritual?
bibl.seg: Christopher A. Faraone, A Wax Effigy Pierced by Three Bones: The Pharaonic Origins of a Late-Antique Cursing Ritual?
bibl.note: A unique recipe preserved in Suppl. Mag. II, 97 (= LDAB 7107) directs the reader on how to make a wax "voodoo doll" and pierce it with three bones of an εισφατη: this word is probably a local and previously unknown Egyptian term for the Nile catfish, with its three distinctive nail-like spines. This can be compared with a native Egyptian cursing ritual of Pharaonic date.
